from.place: The resolution-section comparison: normalized Hom cocycles, their restriction, and their augmentation-preserving pullback transfer, below the Mayer-Vietoris comparison. Substep: whole-to-open restriction of normalized comparisons.

title: Whole to open restriction of canonical resolution comparison
statement: Let X be a scheme, G an abelian sheaf on its small etale site, I an injective resolution of G, and c a resolution-section comparison normalized on Hom cocycles [def-weil-pbc-etale-resolution-section-canonical-comparison]. For every open W of X, natural-number degree q, and class x in H^q(I(X)), applying c.openEquiv W q after homology of section restriction X to W equals cohomologyMap W.ι G q applied after c.globalEquiv q [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback].

proof.text: Evaluate I at the terminal etale object to obtain K. Since K.homologyπ q is an epimorphism in AddCommGrpCat, choose a cycle z representing x. The constant-sheaf adjunction, followed by evaluation at 1 in the lifted integers, gives a morphism f with section K.iCycles q z. Naturality of the adjunction in the coefficient sheaf and K.iCycles_d show f is a Hom cocycle. This uses AddCommGrpCat.epi_iff_surjective and HomologicalComplex.iCycles_d from Mathlib.

Define a from the free abelian sheaf on W to the constant integer sheaf using the sections adjunction applied to the restriction of the global section classifying the identity of the constant integer sheaf. Naturality of sectionsEquiv and of f identifies the section of a composed with f with the restriction of the section of f. HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap_i and homologyπ_naturality identify the restricted cycle and its class. Apply the open_cocycle and global_cocycle normalizations of c.

Prove etaleOpenFreeSheafUnit W followed by upperStar W.ι of a equals the inverse constant-sheaf comparison. Apply the constant-sheaf adjunction on W and evaluate at 1. Naturality of the inverse localization comparison moves a to the original free sheaf; naturality of toSheafify shows its value on the identity generator is the restriction of the global constant section 1. On the other side, constantSection_adjunct_pullback applied to the identity of the integer sheaf expresses the adjunct as this global section followed by the inverse-image unit and terminalSectionPullback. The pointwise localization-unit equation follows directly from Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app and the site map/pullback adjunction. Its adjunct site map equals the composite from the localized terminal object through W to the terminal object of X by terminal uniqueness. Cancel the localization comparison with its inverse to obtain the same section on both sides. This proof needs no nonemptiness assumption.

Rewrite I.extMk of a composed with f using InjectiveResolution.mk₀_comp_extMk. Expand etaleOpenObjectCohomologyMap, use Ext.mapExactFunctor_comp and mapExactFunctor_mk₀, and combine the two degree-zero precompositions using Ext.mk₀_comp_mk₀_assoc. The generator equality just proved replaces their composite with the inverse constant-sheaf comparison. The result is exactly cohomologyMap_apply. These identities hold for every natural-number degree, including zero, and every open, including the empty open.

lean.statement: theorem resolutionSection_canonical_whole_to_open {X : Scheme.{u}} (G : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (I : InjectiveResolution G) (c : ResolutionSectionCanonicalComparison G I) : ∀ W q x, c.openEquiv W q (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (etaleSectionMap (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk W.ι (Category.comp_id _) : Scheme.Etale.mk W.ι ⟶ Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X)) I.cocomplex) q x) = cohomologyMap W.ι G q (c.globalEquiv q x)
